newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed lower across the board on Thursday on moderate retail and interbank interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly again today following another hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a dealer said.

Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.45/98.50 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.52/98.57, September 2001 at S$96.20/96.30 against S$96.30/96.40 and June 2003 at S$94.13/94.18 from S$94.37/94.42.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-3/4 3-5/8 percent versus Wednesday's 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.88/2.83 percent against Wednesday's yield of 2.77/2.72 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.78/2.73 percent from 2.72/2.67 percent.
